findings.text: SPROM revision 4 defines four per-core power table bases at displacements 0x0080, 0x00AE, 0x00DC and 0x010A. Relative to each base, slot 0x00 combines 2 GHz maximum power with its calibration value, slots 0x02, 0x04, 0x06 and 0x08 hold four 2 GHz amplifier values, slot 0x0A combines 5 GHz maximum with its calibration value, slot 0x0C combines 5.2 and 5.8 GHz maxima, slots 0x0E through 0x14 hold four 5.3 GHz amplifier values, slots 0x16 through 0x1C hold four 5.2 GHz amplifier values, and slots 0x1E through 0x24 hold four 5.8 GHz amplifier values. Each combined maximum and calibration word stores maximum in the low byte selected by mask 0x00FF and calibration value in the high byte selected by mask 0xFF00 with an eight bit shift, and the split high-low maximum word stores the high sub-band maximum in the low byte and the low sub-band maximum in the high byte with the same shift.

Legacy revision 4 path 1 entries place the 2 GHz maximum and calibration word at absolute offset 0x0080 and the 5 GHz maximum and calibration word at 0x008A. Each word stores maximum in the low byte under mask 0x00FF and calibration value in the high byte under mask 0xFF00 with an eight bit shift. Six amplifier words are assigned as guesses at 0x0082, 0x0084 and 0x0086 for the first path and 0x008E, 0x0090 and 0x0092 for the second path.

SPROM revision 5 places country code at 0x0044 with two bytes, low board flags at 0x004A, high board flags at 0x004C, second low board flags at 0x004E, second high board flags at 0x0050, and a six byte wireless MAC at 0x0052. General purpose pins 0 and 1 share word 0x0076 with pin 0 in the low byte under mask 0x00FF and pin 1 in the high byte under mask 0xFF00 extracted with shift 8, while pins 2 and 3 share word 0x0078 with the same low and high byte packing and shift.

SPROM revision 8 board identity block starts with board revision at 0x0082, four board flag words at 0x0084 through 0x008A covering bits 0 through 63, six byte MAC at 0x008C and two byte country code at 0x0092. Pins 0 and 1 share word 0x0096 and pins 2 and 3 share word 0x0098, each with low pin under mask 0x00FF and high pin under mask 0xFF00 with shift 8. LED duty word at 0x009A stores off count under mask 0x00FF with shift 0 and on count under mask 0xFF00 with shift 8. Antenna availability at 0x009C stores B and G field under mask 0x00FF with shift 0 and A field under mask 0xFF00 with shift 8. Antenna gains at 0x009E and 0x00A0 store antennas 0 through 3 as alternating low and high bytes under the same byte masks with shifts 0 and 8 in decibel fixed point. Chain control at 0x00A2 stores transmit chains under mask 0x000F, receive chains under mask 0x00F0 with shift 4, and switch control under mask 0xFF00 with shift 8.

Revision 8 radio calibration continues with 2 GHz signal strength parameters at 0x00A4 and 5 GHz parameters at 0x00A6, each combining a low nibble mask 0x000F with fields under masks 0x00F0, 0x0700 and 0x1800 extracted with shifts 4, 8 and 11. Transmit isolation words at 0x00A8 and 0x00AA split low versus high bands between low byte mask 0x00FF and high byte mask 0xFF00 with shift 8. Receive power offsets at 0x00AC use the same low and high byte masks with shifts 0 and 8 for 2 and 5 GHz. Front end module words at 0x00AE and 0x00B0 share masks 0x0001, 0x0006, 0x00F8, 0x0700 and 0xF800 with shifts 0, 1, 3, 8 and 11. Thermal word at 0x00B2 splits offset and threshold between low and high bytes under masks 0x00FF and 0xFF00 with shifts 0 and 8.

Revision 8 temperature words place raw sensor data at 0x00B4 and correction options at 0x00B6. The raw word stores a nine bit temperature under mask 0x01FF with shift 0 and a seven bit measured power field under mask 0xFE00 with shift 9. The correction word stores slope in the low byte under mask 0x00FF with shift 0, a two bit temperature option under mask 0x0300 with shift 8, and receive correction under mask 0xFC00 with shift 10.

Revision 8 calibration control at 0x00B8 packs frequency correction under mask 0x000F with shift 0, a single swap indicator bit under mask 0x0010 with shift 4, and a hardware calibration enable bit under mask 0x0020 with shift 5. Temperature delta policy at 0x00BC packs a low byte calibration threshold under mask 0x00FF with shift 0, a four bit period under mask 0x0F00 with shift 8, and a four bit hysteresis under mask 0xF000 with shift 12.

Revision 8 power tables use four per-core bases at 0x00C0, 0x00E0, 0x0100 and 0x0120. Relative to each base, slot 0x00 combines 2 GHz maximum with calibration value, slots 0x02, 0x04 and 0x06 hold three 2 GHz amplifier values, slot 0x08 combines 5 GHz maximum with calibration value, slot 0x0A combines 5.2 and 5.8 GHz maxima, slots 0x0C through 0x10 hold three 5.3 GHz amplifier values, slots 0x12 through 0x16 hold three 5.2 GHz amplifier values, and slots 0x18 through 0x1C hold three 5.8 GHz amplifier values. Combined words use low byte mask 0x00FF for maximum and high byte mask 0xFF00 for calibration value with shift 8, and the split maximum word uses low byte for high band and high byte for low band with the same shift.

Revision 8 path 1 absolute power entries place 2 GHz maximum and calibration at 0x00C0, three 2 GHz amplifier words at 0x00C2, 0x00C4 and 0x00C6, 5.3 GHz maximum and calibration at 0x00C8, split 5.2 and 5.8 GHz maxima at 0x00CA, three 5.3 GHz amplifier words at 0x00CC, 0x00CE and 0x00D0, three 5.2 GHz amplifier words at 0x00D2, 0x00D4 and 0x00D6, and three 5.8 GHz amplifier words at 0x00D8, 0x00DA and 0x00DC. Combined words use low byte mask 0x00FF for maximum and high byte mask 0xFF00 for calibration value with shift 8, and the split word uses low byte for 5.8 GHz and high byte for 5.2 GHz with the same shift.

Revision 8 power offset tables use absolute bases at 0x0140 for CCK, 0x0142 for 2.4 GHz OFDM, 0x0146 for 5.3 GHz OFDM, 0x014A for 5.2 GHz OFDM and 0x014E for 5.8 GHz OFDM, followed by modulation coding rate tables at 0x0152, 0x0162, 0x0172 and 0x0182 for 2, 5.3, 5.2 and 5.8 GHz, and shared adjustment words at 0x0192, 0x0194, 0x0196 and 0x0198 for cyclic delay diversity, space time block coding, 40 MHz bandwidth and duplicate bandwidth modes.

Low board capability word encodes sixteen single-bit features as successive powers of two from 0x0001 through 0x8000. In ascending bit order they report Bluetooth coexistence, GPIO PA control, airline radio disable indication, software slope calculation, Ethernet SPI switch, absent slow crystal, high power CCK, ADM switch presence, VLAN support, Afterburner support, floating PCI, front end module support, external amplifier, high gain PA, alternate coexistence GPIOs and alternate IQ configuration.

High board capability word encodes seven single-bit features as masks 0x0001 through 0x0040. In ascending order they report missing PA, positive slope signal strength, PA reference regulator use, triple throw Bluetooth switch, phase shifter support, buck booster presence and shared Bluetooth front end module with antenna switch.

Second board capability word encodes eleven single-bit features as masks 0x0001 through 0x0400. In ascending order they report external baseband regulator, alternate A band PLL workaround, transmit power control permission, two by four diversity switch, 5 GHz power gain, PCI express workaround override, reserved board marker, three wire Bluetooth coexistence, Skyworks module board, clock spur workaround and alternate G band PLL workaround.

Revision 1 country code enumeration assigns successive integer codes starting at zero for world, then Thailand, Israel, Jordan, China, Japan, USA Canada Australia New Zealand group, Europe, USA low, Japan high, all and none, giving twelve ordered regulatory selectors.

Sonics address descriptor packs type in low two bits under mask 0x00000003 with values 0, 1 and 2, a 64 bit address flag as bit 2, size fields under masks 0x000000F8 for type 0 and 0x000001F8 for types 1 and 2 with shift 3, enable as bit 10 and negative decode as bit 11. Base addresses use mask 0xFFFFFF00 with shift 8 for type 0, mask 0xFFFFF000 with shift 12 for type 1, and mask 0xFFFF0000 with shift 16 for type 2.
Stack protector header is guarded by a single inclusion macro that marks the header as already processed.

Stack canary mask takes one of three build specific values, two 64 bit forms that clear the low byte or the high byte and one 32 bit all-ones form, namely 0xffffffffffffff00UL, 0x00ffffffffffffffUL and 0xffffffffUL, so any masked random canary carries a terminating zero byte.
Exposes a helper that supplies a fresh stack canary derived from the kernel random source and constrained by the configured canary mask.
Provides a boot time canary initialization entry that performs no action in this configuration.
Stack trace header is guarded by a single inclusion macro marking it as already processed.
Defines a stack unwinding callback contract that receives an opaque cookie plus a program address and returns whether iteration should continue.
Stack trace carrier holds a filled count and a capacity, a pointer to an address array, and an input skip count indicating how many initial entries to discard.
Provides a fallback for reliable per-task stack capture that signals absence of architecture support by returning negative ENOSYS.
Callers must handle the not-supported result from reliable per-task capture and must not treat missing output as a successful trace.
Start kernel header is guarded by a single inclusion macro marking it as already processed.
Variable argument handling exposes a list type plus start, end, fetch and copy operations, each forwarded to the corresponding compiler builtin for the current calling convention.
Standard definition header is guarded by a single inclusion macro marking it as already processed.
Null pointer constant is a void pointer to address zero, and the boolean enumeration assigns zero to false and one to true.
Member displacement query yields the compile-time byte offset of a member within its type, and the end variant adds the member size to obtain the offset just past that member.
Grouping macro lets a declaration bundle several members under one name by forwarding to an internal grouping helper.
